graphEvents.label: Which gates judge an embedded skill
Pair declarations live in a third shared file

label: The parity gate is shared and external: it lives in AI Systems/z — Claude Project Sync Loop, and PO's benchmark/parity holds five thin wrappers that pass a system id or directory and exec into it.
Pair declarations come from the shared systems.py, which holds 38 pairs for product-owner; a new skill-to-knowledge pair must be declared there, a third surface beyond the two repositories.
Rule parity counts verbatim spans on both sides of every declared pair with a per-rule floor, so a new mirrored rule needs a grep-stable span and a floor rather than a paraphrase.
Example lint validates every worked example and every Project example mirror plus each worked reply's required lines, so a new mode with examples inherits that shape contract.
Receipts are a required check: a missing or stale dated upload receipt is a finding under --receipts, so a green gate never proves deployment.
The shared residency check holds every declared kernel statement to the kernel or its declared home, so moving a rule into a new knowledge document requires updating the declaration.
